why:
REFUTED on four independent grounds. The quote is real and the two cited lines say what was claimed, but the row is a duplicate of an already-adjudicated finding, it is a dated parked owner decision, its stated mechanism is factually wrong, and BOTH halves of the claimed exposure are already delivered one layer up. 1) QUOTE — CONFIRMED VERBATIM, and the whole line carries no reversing second half. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w26.md` line 53 is a single-item grid cell in the 'Other wins' section: `
New sandbox.credentials setting blocks sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables
`. Stripping the `` markup gives the claimed sentence character-for-character. One sentence, no qualifier. The `files`/`envVars` sub-key claim is independently supported by settings.md:421-:424 (`credentials.files`, `credentials.envVars`, `credentials.envVars[].injectHosts`, `credentials.allowPlaintextInject`). No refutation here. 2) CITED FILE:LINE — accurate on the letter, wrong on the reading. packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:172-180 is exactly `['excludedCommands','deniedReadRoots','deniedWriteRoots','additionalWritableRoots','allowUnsandboxedCommands','network','filesystem']` — no `credentials`. `grep -ran credentials` on that file (NUL-safe) returns only :321 and :324. But the claim that the name appears 'only as a shape ANALOGY … borrowed' framed as a defect inverts what the comments do: :318-327 says '`settings.md:200`\'s `sandbox.credentials` row applied to the sub-block we actually have', a deliberate, argued borrow of the doc's ONLY published nested-block tolerance rule, quoted in full with its reason ('Returning `undefined` for a wholly invalid `network` is what makes the rest of `sandbox` still apply'). managed-policy.ts:1164 states it outright: 'Shaped like `settings.md:200`\'s `sandbox.credentials` row, which is the doc's only nested-document case'. And settings.md:200 really is that row, verbatim. Citing the one published precedent for a tolerance shape is not evidence of a gap. 2b) THE CLAIMED MECHANISM IS WRONG. 'the key is stripped as unknown' is false on the strict path. Ran the real parser: `parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1({credentials:{files:[…],envVars:[…]}})` → `THREW: invalid sandbox setting: credentials` (assertKnownKeys, :216-221). Positive control on the same rig: `parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1({deniedReadRoots:['/Users/x/.aws']})` → parses clean, so the throw is about the key name, not a broken probe. Stripping happens only on the tolerant managed-delivery path. A row whose mechanism is wrong cannot be dispatched as written. 3) OWNER DECISION — this is parity row R19, PARKED. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:690: row R19, status ⏸, scope 'Egress proxy and domain policy: … `mask` mode for named env vars', marked 'PARKED by owner decision 2026-07-28 — «нужно всё разрешить, ограничения будут потом»', with the plan deliberately retained at docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md (:15 'there is no mask/deny path for `credentials.envVars` today — Task 4 adds `deny` there'; :31 lands the documented `mask`-without-`tlsTerminate` failure). docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:218 carries 'R19 — `credentials.envVars` `mask` … Half-shipped, then parked by owner decision — so nothing is live'. Audit :478 records an earlier finder hitting this same row and being told it belonged to R19. Not one of inert-worklist §3's nine (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions), but an equivalent dated owner decision recorded in three places. 4) CONSEQUENCE REFUTED UPSTREAM ON BOTH HALVES (trap shape #3 — the identifier is unwired, the consequence is false). The doc sentence names two protections; this fork ships both unconditionally, by other names, and is STRICTER than a default Claude install on each. (a) CREDENTIAL FILES. `credentialDenyRoots` (packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/credential-deny-roots.ts:96) is a host-seeded, unremovable floor covering the doc's own two examples (~/.ssh, ~/.aws) plus ~/.nessy, ~/.netrc, ~/._netrc, ~/.docker, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.config/git/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.pypirc, ~/.kube, ~/.gnupg, ~/.config/gh, ~/.config/gcloud, ~/.azure, ~/Library/Keychains, the per-vendor browser cookie/login stores and the Windows DPAPI trio. It is seeded into `deniedReadRoots` at packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/host-sandbox-settings.ts:61 and independently at packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/script-sandbox.ts:83, composed into the isolation funnel as `unconditionalDeniedReadRoots` (filesystem-isolation.ts:136-184), and passed as `credentialFloor` at bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:225 so /doctor and the funnel agree. sandbox-settings.ts:708-716 makes a user `filesystem.allowRead` unable to re-open a floor path, and :798-815 RETAINS the floor even when `filesystem.disabled` turns the layer off, with the reason written in-line ('so releasing it here would let one boolean in a user file hand over ~/.ssh, ~/.aws and the gateway token under ~/.nessy'). Claude documents the opposite default at sandboxing.md:271 — 'There is no built-in credential deny list, so only the files and variables you list are restricted' — which credential-deny-roots.ts:20-22 quotes as its rationale. (b) SECRET ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES. This half was NOT covered by the earlier sibling verdict and I verified it directly. Supervised processes get their host env through `hostEnvironment(profile)` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:726-732), and the DEFAULT profile is `restricted` (`resolveEnvironmentProfile` :716-724 — `restricted` unless a caller explicitly asks otherwise). `restricted` is an ALLOWLIST, not a deny list: `RESTRICTED_HOST_ENVIRONMENT` (:703-711) admits 25 names plus an `LC_*` pattern — HOME/PATH/SHELL/USER/LOGNAME, locale and terminal vars, toolchain roots, the Windows quartet, and four NESSY_* doc-path vars. Nothing else from process.env crosses. So AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and NESSY_DP_AUTH_TOKEN are absent from a sandboxed command's environment by construction. `grep -ran "'trusted-host'"` over production source returns only the type declaration, the two enum validators and the supervisor's own comparison — no production caller requests it, and no bash path sets `inheritHostEnv: true` (local-tools/runtime.ts:398-404 is `processBinding`, a result-REPORTING projection back onto the observability record, not a start request). Claude's default is the inverse: the whole environment passes unless a variable is named in `credentials.envVars`. So what is absent is the CONFIGURABILITY — an administrator cannot name extra files or extra variables, and `mask` (which needs the TLS-terminating proxy R19 parked) has no analogue. The protection the doc sentence describes is not absent; it is on by default and not removable. 5) NOT a brand/gateway/subscription product difference — this is a settings-schema question, not renaming. 6) PROVENANCE. This row is the whats-new restatement of docs/superpowers/specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json:3573-3574, and its `sandboxing.md` twin (phase1 :388-390) was already challenged and REFUTED in docs/superpowers/specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase2-partial.json on grounds 3 and 4(a). I re-derived both from source rather than inheriting them, and added 4(b), the env-var half that verdict left as the one unrefuted piece.
correctedState:
`sandbox.credentials` is unimplemented as a settings key, deliberately and on the record — and the settings surface REFUSES it rather than stripping it: `parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1({credentials:{…}})` throws `invalid sandbox setting: credentials` (packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:172-180 + :216-221); stripping-with-a-warning happens only on the tolerant managed-delivery path. It is parity row R19 (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:690), status ⏸, PARKED by owner decision 2026-07-28 («нужно всё разрешить, ограничения будут потом»), plan retained at docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md (Task 4 = `credentials.envVars` `deny`; `mask` deliberately fail-closed pending TLS termination), with the `mask` half recorded as parked at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:218.

Both protections the doc sentence names nevertheless ship, unconditionally and under other names, and a default Nessy install is stricter than a default Claude install on each:

- Credential FILES — `credentialDenyRoots` (packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/credential-deny-roots.ts:96) seeds `deniedReadRoots` on every sandboxed command via host-sandbox-settings.ts:61 and script-sandbox.ts:83, enters the funnel as `unconditionalDeniedReadRoots` (filesystem-isolation.ts:136-184), outranks any `filesystem.allowRead` (sandbox-settings.ts:708-716) and survives `filesystem.disabled` (:798-815). Covers ~/.ssh and ~/.aws — the doc's own examples — plus ~/.nessy, ~/.gnupg, ~/.kube, ~/.docker, ~/.npmrc, ~/.pypirc, ~/.netrc, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.config/{git/credentials,gh,gcloud}, ~/.azure, ~/Library/Keychains, browser cookie/login stores and the Windows DPAPI trio. Claude ships none by default (sandboxing.md:271).
- Secret ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES — supervised processes default to the `restricted` environment profile (process-supervisor.ts:716-724), and `hostEnvironment` (:726-732) filters process.env through the `RESTRICTED_HOST_ENVIRONMENT` ALLOWLIST (:703-711): 25 names plus `LC_*`. No production caller requests `trusted-host`. Every secret variable is therefore absent from a sandboxed command's environment by construction, where Claude passes the whole environment unless a variable is named.

The genuine, recorded residual is configurability, not exposure: an administrator cannot extend either list through settings, and `mask` (sentinel substitution, which requires the TLS-terminating egress proxy R19 parked) has no analogue at all. Unparking R19 is what closes it.
